presentation: A 71-year-old woman with no prior lung disease develops productive cough episodes lasting more than four weeks almost every year, usually after a presumed viral illness. She denies wheezing; her chest X-ray is normal, PFTs are pending, and she has a history of GERD managed with famotidine (PPIs were tried without relief). In the past, a short course of azithromycin temporarily relieved the cough, but it always recurs. Should I continue empirically prescribing azithromycin each time she coughs given the prior improvement?
